{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./bead-select.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from PBS:
#   -l procs=1            -> -n 1
#   -l walltime=100:00:00 -> -t 100h
#   -t 0-1024             -> submit 1025 jobs (0..1024) (best-effort via flux submit --cc)

# NOTE: PBS -l mem=7GB not translated.
# Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, jobs may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

# NOTE: PBS -q WitsLong not translated.
# Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, jobs may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the WitsLong queue.

# NOTE: PBS -N bead-select not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

START=0
END=1024
COUNT=$((END-START+1))

# Submit array jobs; each task uses its rank as an index, shifted by START.
# (This requires that `flux submit --cc` is available in your Flux installation.)
flux submit --cc=${COUNT} -n 1 -t 100h \
  bash -lc 'IDX=${FLUX_TASK_RANK:-0}; PBS_ARRAYID=$(( '"$START"' + IDX )); \
    hostname; \
    cd /spaces/scott/chip/pool_selection/ || exit 1; \
    run=${PBS_ARRAYID}; \
    /usr/bin/time python pool_select.py --input all.cpickle --label S${LABEL} --bad badscore60.lst --requests extra.lst,req_func_u.scores --factor 1.5 ${run} 10 18'
"
}
